title: Micelle-Driven MOF Degradation for Enhanced Cargo Release in Micromotors
abstract: Abstract Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are widely explored as cargo-delivery platforms, yet efficient release of the encapsulated cargo remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate that anionic surfactant micelles actively destabilize the HKUST-1 MOF framework through Cu2+ extraction, converting a typically undesired degradation process into a mechanism for enhanced cargo release. Complementary mechanistic studies reveal that this process depends on surfactant self-assembly and on the accessibility and coordination environment of the metal nodes. The resulting framework destabilization greatly enhances the release of different cargos from HKUST-1. This mechanistic concept is subsequently translated into tubular MOF-based micromotors by confining SDS within an agarose matrix inside the micromotor cavity. Local surfactant release generates a micelle-rich microenvironment that promotes MOF degradation and cargo release while limiting bulk surfactant exposure and reducing the cytotoxic effects associated with free surfactant under the tested conditions. The resulting platform integrates micelle-mediated MOF disassembly with spatially confined micromotor delivery, providing a strategy for localized and enhanced cargo release from MOF-based dynamic systems.

title: Interfacial molecular gateway via supramolecular assembly on metal–organic framework for highly selective CO 2 separation
abstract: Abstract Adsorptive CO 2 separation from industrial gas offers an energy‐efficient approach for carbon capture, but is restricted by simultaneously achieving high adsorption capacity and selectivity. Herein, we report an interfacial molecular gateway engineering strategy on metal–organic framework that enhances selective CO 2 transport while preserving intrinsic framework porosity. A supramolecular assembly approach was developed to construct a robust imidazolium polymer shell on mesoporous MIL‐101(Cr) through supramolecular interactions, circumventing pore‐blocking limitations commonly encountered in core–shell architectures. Benefiting from synergy between electrostatic and hydrogen‐bonding attractions in the shell and efficient molecular transport in the core, the heterostructure exhibits IAST selectivities of 1029 for CO 2 /N 2 and 97 for CO 2 /CH 4 , while nearly doubling the CO 2 adsorption capacity of MIL‐101(Cr). This enables direct production of high‐purity CO 2 (>99 vol.%) from simulated flue gas and natural gas. This work establishes a versatile interfacial engineering platform for porous frameworks, providing a promising route toward high‐performance adsorbents for industrial gas purification.

title: Polarity‐Directed Assembly of in‐Plane Oriented Covalent Organic Framework Films on Substrates
abstract: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional (2D) covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs) are promising crystalline porous materials for optoelectronic applications; however, controlled growth of COF thin films on substrates remains a significant challenge. Here, we develop a polarity‐directed solution assembly strategy for the fabrication of 2D COF thin films on various substrates. This approach leverages polarity‐driven solvent–molecule interactions to regulate precursor assembly and oriented polymerization, successfully yielding in‐plane oriented COF films with controllable thickness, smooth surface morphology, and abundant nitrogen active sites. When these films are used as templates for perovskite growth, the resulting heterojunction interfaces effectively passivate buried interfacial defects and suppress non‐radiative recombination. Integrated into light‐emitting diodes (LED), the devices achieve a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 30.88%, a peak luminance of 1.7 × 10 5 cd/m 2 , and an operational half‐lifetime (T 50 ) of 12.74 h at an initial luminance of 9206 cd/m 2 (equivalent to >6238 h at 100 cd/m 2 ), surpassing most previously reported counterparts. This work opens a new molecular regulation avenue toward the preparation of highly oriented COF films for versatile optoelectronic applications.

title: Hierarchically Porous Metal–Organic Frameworks as Multifunctional Platforms for Synergistic Chemo-Photo-Biocatalytic Enantioselective Synthesis
abstract: Abstract Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer a promising platform for the precise customization of multifunctional composites, enabling the optimization of synergistic effects between catalysts and significantly enhancing both stability and catalytic performance. Despite this potential, this idealized system is still in the exploratory stage. Herein, we integrated a chemical catalyst with a photoenzyme-based enantioselective catalytic platform into a single system, achieving the sequential transformation from C2-alkylation to asymmetric Mannich reaction products. A hierarchically porous (HP) UiO-67 material was constructed as the supporting platform. Through a post-synthetic ligand exchange strategy, Pd(II) and Ru(II) catalysts were simultaneously immobilized, while wheat germ lipase (WGL) was encapsulated within the mesoporous channels, yielding the multifunctional catalyst WGL@HP-UiO-67-Pd/Ru. This catalyst afforded satisfactory yields of 62–94% in the C2-arylation reaction and enantioselectivities of 69–93% in the asymmetric Mannich reaction. In this sequential catalytic transformation, the multifunctional catalyst afforded an overall efficiency of 47.6%, corresponding to a 3.8-fold enhancement over the homogeneous catalyst system. These findings provide deeper insight into the role of multifunctional catalysis in sequential reactions and underscore its considerable promise for the asymmetric synthesis of organic compounds and pharmaceutical agents.

title: Tuning Fatty Acid-Templated Mesoporous Silica for Adsorption and Hemocompatibility
abstract: Abstract Mesoporous silica was synthesized via a green sol–gel route using biosourced C16–C18 fatty acid mixtures as structure-directing agents. Tuning the silica precursor, solvent, and pH allowed precise control over the interfacial self-assembly, shifting the template state from encapsulated free fatty acids (acidic) to saponified soap micelles (basic). The optimized fumed silica/NaOH sample (ST4) exhibited exceptional textural properties, featuring a high surface area (958 m²·g⁻¹), large pore volume (0.89 cm³·g⁻¹), and a predominantly mesoporous character (79%) with a highly ordered hexagonal structure. This tailored architecture enabled efficient, balanced adsorption of small blood biomolecules (urea, creatinine, and glucose) while demonstrating excellent hemocompatibility (< 3% hemolysis, ISO 10993-4). These findings highlight the potential of eco-friendly, fatty acid-templated mesoporous silica as a highly effective and biocompatible platform for blood purification and biomedical applications.

title: Metal‐Phenolic Nanoplatforms: Zinc‐Loaded Mesoporous Catechin Microneedles for Multi‐Mechanistic Healing of Diabetic Oral Ulcers
abstract: Diabetic oral ulcers remain challenging to treat due to persistent inflammation, bacterial infection, and impaired regeneration. Herein, we report mesoporous catechin nanospheres (MCNs) as a versatile platform for multi‐metal ion delivery and their integration into a microneedle (MN) patch for ulcer therapy. MCNs, synthesized via interfacial assembly, exhibit high surface area and well‐defined mesoporosity, enabling efficient coordination with a broad range of therapeutic metal ions, including but not limited to Zn 2 +, Sr 2 +, Cu 2 +, and Mn 2 +. Zinc‐coordinated MCNs (Zn@MCNs) demonstrate pH‐responsive release, enabling on‐demand delivery within the acidic wound microenvironment. When loaded into dissolvable gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) microneedles (MN‐Zn@MCNs), the patch achieves effective mucosal penetration and sustained drug release. In vitro and in vivo studies reveal that MN‐Zn@MCNs exhibit immunomodulation by promoting M2 macrophage polarization, broad‐spectrum antibacterial activity, and potent reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging. In a diabetic rat model, the patch significantly accelerates ulcer closure, re‐epithelialization, angiogenesis, and collagen deposition. Transcriptomic analysis implicates regulation of the PI3K‐Akt pathway. This work establishes MCNs as a metal‐phenolic nanoplatform for multimodal ion delivery, offering a promising strategy for diabetic oral ulcer management and a versatile blueprint for next‐generation wound healing materials.

title: Ytterbium Metal‐Organic Framework With DNA Hydrogel Switching for ElectroChemiluminescence Biosensing
abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional electrochemiluminescence (ECL) biosensors typically rely on stepwise assembly of recognition probes and signal labels directly on electrode surfaces, which suffers from severe fouling and poor reproducibility when dealing with crude plant extracts. Here, we discover that a pre‐reduction treatment at −3 V boosts the cathodic ECL of an ytterbium metal‐organic framework (Yb‐MOF) by 14‐fold through a radical‐accumulation mechanism. Leveraging this emitter, we construct a spatially decoupled biosensor that physically separates target recognition from signal transduction using a DNA hydrogel. In a test tube, CRISPR‐Cas12a activated by the Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus outer membrane protein ( C Las Omp) gene cleaves a rolling circle amplification derived DNA hydrogel, releasing encapsulated Fe 3 O 4 nanolabels. After magnetic separation, these labels are simply dropped onto the Yb‐MOF electrode, inducing ECL quenching via resonance energy transfer (RET). The ECL change (ΔECL) exhibits a linear relationship with the target concentration over the range of 10 pM to 100 nM, affording a detection limit of 2 pM. Moreover, the sensor demonstrates single‐base mismatch discrimination. The spatial decoupling strategy provides a robust paradigm for plant pathogen surveillance in complex agricultural matrices.

title: Alloying‐Phase‐Regulated ZnO@C Scaffolds for Uniform and Pore‐Filling Lithium Metal Deposition
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium metal anodes deliver ultrahigh theoretical capacity, yet dendrite growth, unstable interfaces and drastic volume expansion hinder battery practicalization. The 3D lithiophilic skeleton has become an effective strategy to homogenize lithium deposition; nevertheless, spatially nonuniform nucleation still occurs on insufficiently modified regions, while the loading amount of lithiophilic components is commonly optimized by empirical trial‐and‐error rather than by a clear structure‐phase‐deposition relationship. Herein, we construct flower‐like 3D porous ZnO@C scaffolds assembled from 2D nanosheets, which integrates uniformly distributed ZnO‐derived lithiophilic sites, an interconnected carbon‐conductive network, and abundant internal pore space, thereby coupling alloying‐regulated Li nucleation with pore‐confined Li accommodation. The optimized ZnO@C‐25% electrode achieves dendrite‐free cycling over 1200 h with an ultra‐low voltage hysteresis of 37 mV. When paired with LFP and NMC‐811 cathodes, the full cells deliver outstanding cycling stability and high energy‐power output. Operando transmission XRD combined with DFT calculations reveals the sequential Li‐Zn alloy phase evolution, and in situ formed LiZn phase dominates favorable epitaxial Li growth due to strong Li affinity and fast Li diffusion capability. This work establishes a mechanistic correlation among controllable lithiophilic loading, dynamic alloy‐phase evolution, and pore‐filling Li storage behavior, offering a rational design principle for 3D hosts toward high‐energy lithium metal batteries.

title: An Ionic Hydrogen-Bonded Organic Framework Exhibiting Dual Emission and Photochromism Mediated by Photoinduced Electron Transfer
abstract: Abstract Hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HOFs) have attracted significant attention in the field of photofunctional materials due to their structural tunability and dynamic response properties; however, the synergistic integration of room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) and photochromic activity remains a challenge. In this study, iHOF-72 was synthesized via self-assembly of 1,5-naphthalenedisulfonic acid (1,5-NDSA) as the building block and tris(4-pyridyl)amine (TPA) using the solvent evaporation method. The study found that iHOF-72 exhibits fluorescence at 409 nm and RTP emission at 565 nm, with a total photoluminescence quantum yield as high as 89.3%. Furthermore, when exposed to 365 nm UV light in the solid state, iHOF-72 exhibits significant photochromic behavior, which quenches the RTP emission. Optical characterization and theoretical calculations have confirmed that the radical (TPA•) generated by photoinduced electron transfer (PET) exhibits a significant quenching effect on triplet excitons. Here, a flexible film (X %-iHOF-72@PVA) was prepared by compositing iHOF-72 with polyvinyl alcohol (PVA). The rigid constraints provided by the PVA matrix effectively suppressed non-radiative transitions, significantly enhancing the yellow-green afterglow of the composite film while preserving its rapid photochromic response characteristics. Based on the differences in afterglow observed in multi-scale composite films, a “lotus flower” pattern was successfully fabricated, providing new material design concepts for time-domain information display in flexible smart optoelectronic devices and for multi-level information encryption.

title: Self-assembly of monovalent anion pillared metal-organic frameworks: linker functionalization matters
abstract: Monovalent anion pillaring in coordination networks remains a challenging design target because charge balance requires the simultaneous incorporation of additional counteranions within the structure. Here, we show that subtle changes in the substitution pattern of bis(imidazolyl)benzene (bib) linkers can strongly alter the outcome of self-assembly in Cu(II)-based systems with monovalent polyatomic anions. The dimethoxy-substituted ligand 1,1'-(2,5-dimethoxy-1,4-phenylene)bis(1H-imidazole) (bib(OMe)2) reacts with Cu(BF4)2, Cu(ClO4)2 and Cu(NO3)2 to afford three isoreticular monovalent anion-pillared frameworks, {Cu[bib(OMe)2]2X}X (X = BF4−, UdP-30; ClO4−, UdP-31; NO3−, UdP-32), in which Cu-bib(OMe)2 layers are connected by coordinated anions while additional charge-balancing anions are located within the pores. The frameworks crystallize in the monoclinic C2/c space group and differ from previously reported bibCF3-based topological analogues (UdP-10, -11, and -12, containing the same anions) in symmetry, layer geometry, anion arrangement, and pore accessibility. These compounds retain crystallinity upon desolvation and possess accessible microporosity, as evidenced by gas sorption analysis.

title: Regioswitchable and Enantioselective Dialkylation of Alkenes: Modular Access to Chiral β- and γ-Amino Esters
abstract: Abstract Catalytic alkene difunctionalization is a powerful strategy for the rapid assembly of complex molecular architectures and has wide applications in synthetic chemistry. However, selective construction of two distinct alkyl–alkyl bonds across the C═C bond in alkenes remains a formidable challenge. Existing methods heavily rely on directing group strategy or specific ground-state radical traps, and the regio- and enantioselective dialkylation of alkenes remains elusive. Furthermore, a method enabling the simultaneous access to two regioisomers in an enantioselective manner has not yet been devised. Herein, we present a regioswitchable and enantioselective alkene dialkylation via photoredox/nickel dual catalysis. This approach provides a unique technique for the modular and practical synthesis of optically pure natural and unnatural β- and γ-amino esters, cornerstones of chemistry and biology. This method utilizes readily available and abundant unactivated alkyl halides and protic C(sp3)–H bonds as coupling partners, demonstrating broad substrate applicability as well as excellent regio- and enantioselectivity. The key to the success lies in the ingenious utilization of the rate difference in the generation of alkyl radicals between alkyl iodides and alkyl bromides via halogen-atom transfer. Furthermore, the synthetic practicality of this regiodivergent protocol has been demonstrated in the enantioselective synthesis of pharmaceutically relevant molecules.

title: Stepwise Assembly of a Lavandulyl Moiety on Flavonoids Enabled by a 2″-Prenyltransferase
abstract: Abstract Lavandulylated flavonoids contain a characteristic branched C10 moiety, and the enzymatic basis underlying its biosynthesis remains poorly understood. Here, we elucidate the complete biosynthetic pathway of the lavandulylated flavonoid kurarinone from naringenin in the medicinal plant Sophora flavescens. The pathway involves four sequential steps, 8-prenylation, 2′-hydroxylation, 2″-prenylation, and 5-O-methylation, catalyzed by Sf8PT, SfF2′H, Sf2″PT, and Sf5OMT, respectively. Sf2′′PT represents the first characterized flavonoid 2′′-prenyltransferase (PT), catalyzing a second prenylation on the pre-existing prenyl side chain to complete the assembly of the branched lavandulyl moiety. The activity of Sf2″PT strictly depends on prior 2′-hydroxylation, establishing a defined order of enzymatic modifications that enables this noncanonical prenylation reaction. Ancestral sequence reconstruction and mutagenesis demonstrated that an inactive ancestral enzyme could be converted into functional 8PT or 2′′PT variants through one or seven amino acid substitutions, respectively. Collectively, this work establishes the enzymatic basis for stepwise lavandulyl moiety assembly and provides a framework for the enzymatic construction and engineering of branched prenylated natural products.

title: Synthetic Control of Quantum Phases in Organic Conductors: Molecular-Level Disorder Engineering and Pressure-Induced Superconductivity
abstract: Abstract Structural randomness is a dominant factor governing electronic properties; however, the intrinsic effects of a disordered potential remain elusive due to the lack of a synthetic platform capable of introducing purely random potentials without carrier doping or altering the fundamental band structure. Here, we demonstrate the synthetic control of superconducting and insulating phases by exploiting the unique conformational flexibility of molecular conductors. Through precise thermodynamic control during crystal growth, we selectively synthesize the structurally ordered superconductor κ-(BEDT-TTF)2Cu[N(CN)2]Br (κ-Br; BEDT-TTF = bis(ethylenedithio)tetrathiafulvalene) and the structurally disordered insulating polymorph, κ″-(BEDT-TTF)2Cu[N(CN)2]Br (κ″-Br), possessing the exact same chemical composition. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm the metastable nature of κ″-Br, showing a packing arrangement of BEDT-TTF molecules and an electronic band structure nearly identical to those of superconducting κ-Br, but featuring a disordered anion layer. Optical conductivity spectra reveal low-energy excitations without a distinct gap, indicating that the insulating behavior originates from disorder-induced carrier localization. Furthermore, κ″-Br undergoes a pressure-induced insulator–superconductor transition, in stark contrast to postsynthetic X-ray irradiation which induced irreversible structural damage. This work represents the first demonstration of synthetic control of an ordered superconductor and a disordered insulator driven solely by orientational disorder in organic conductors. Our study provides new avenues for manipulating strongly correlated electron systems and for investigating the intrinsic effects of randomness, free from carrier doping or structural perturbation of conducting layers.

title: Chloride‐Induced Microstructure–Covalency Coupling Enables Ultrafine Nanoparticle Exsolution for High‐Performance CO 2 Electrolysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient CO 2 electrolysis in solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) requires active cathode catalysts that combine abundant active interfaces, rapid charge transfer, and long‐term structural stability. Perovskite exsolution can generate robust metal nanoparticles (NPs), but achieving a dense population of ultrafine nanocatalysts remains challenging. Here, we report a chloride‐assisted exsolution strategy in Sr 2 Fe 1.3 Ni 0.2 Mo 0.5 O 6‐δ (SFNM)‐based cathodes, demonstrating for the first time that Cl doping links grain‐boundary (GB) engineering with metal–oxygen covalency regulation to direct FeNi NP exsolution. Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) analysis shows that the SrCl 2 ‐derived molten‐salt flux effect creates a faceted, GB‐rich perovskite morphology, increasing the GB density by approximately 78.9% and providing abundant nucleation sites for exsolution. X‐ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) and theoretical calculations further reveal that Cl substitution attenuates metal–oxygen hybridization, promotes oxygen‐vacancy formation, and facilitates outward segregation of Fe and Ni. This chloride‐triggered dual regulation yields a highly populated FeNi NP surface, accelerating CO 2 electroreduction and lowering polarization resistance. Consequently, the reduced Cl‐doped SFNM cathode (R‐SFNMCl2) achieves 2.73 A cm −2 at 800°C and 1.5 V, while sustaining stable operation for 400 h with only minor degradation. This work establishes a new halogen‐mediated exsolution design paradigm for developing high‐performance SOEC cathode catalysts.

title: Spatially Synchronized Ion‐Electron Transport Enables Millimeter‐Thick Cathodes for Ah‐Level Aqueous Cu‐S Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Thick conversion electrodes are essential for practical high‐energy aqueous batteries, yet their electrochemical reactions become increasingly heterogeneous when ionic and electronic pathways are spatially decoupled across the electrode depth. Here, sulfated cellulose nanofibrils (SCNFs) and PEDOT:PSS are integrated to construct a nanocellulose‐enabled architecture that synchronizes ionic and electronic transport in millimeter‐thick aqueous Cu‐S cathodes. The SCNF framework directs conformal PEDOT:PSS assembly along continuous nanofibrils, creating collocated electronic pathways and hydrophilic Cu 2+ ‐transport channels within one fibrillar scaffold. Electrochemical analysis, Raman mapping, and X‐ray computed tomography reveal that this integrated network converts localized sulfur conversion into a homogeneous and reversible through‐thickness reaction. Consequently, the optimized cathode retains 98.6% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 5 A g −1 and delivers an areal capacity exceeding 179 mAh cm −2 at an ultrahigh sulfur loading of 112 mg cm −2 . In a high‐loading pouch‐cell configuration, the optimized cathode further achieves a capacity of approximately 3 Ah. Furthermore, a decoupled Zn‐S configuration design delivers an energy density of 651 Wh kg −1 based on sulfur and zinc active materials. This work establishes spatial synchronization of ionic and electronic transport as a broadly applicable design principle for practical high‐loading conversion electrodes.

title: Counter-ion confinement reverses ion selectivity in subnanometer channels
abstract: Ion transport in nano- and subnanometer channels is central to processes such as ion separation, energy conversion and storage, and nanofluidics. Conventionally, positively charged nanochannels favor anion transport and vice versa. We report that cationic covalent organic framework membranes with sub–one-nanometer channels exhibit selective cation transport. This reversal in selectivity arises from a counter-ion confinement effect, which inverts the electrostatic environment inside the channel wall and creates a secondary confinement region. The counter-ion confinement mechanism concomitantly suppresses coexisting ion competition in mixed-salt systems, enabling membranes to retain high selectivity under practical separation conditions. Our findings provide a design strategy for creating adaptive and highly selective membranes for precise ion transport and separation.

title: Redox-Window-Guided Metal Node Editing of Copper Metal–Organic Frameworks for Recyclable Heterogeneous Cu(I) Catalysis
abstract: Abstract Cu(I) catalysts are central to many bond-forming reactions, but integrating Cu(I) sites into recyclable porous solids remains difficult because Cu(I) is easily oxidized, over-reduced, or leached. Here, we report redox-window-guided metal node editing as an oxidation-state-programming strategy that converts hydrolytically fragile Cu(II)3BTC2 into a hydrolytically stable mixed-valence Cu(I/II) MOF catalyst. Phenolic reductants are selected by matching their oxidation potentials to the Cu(II)–to–Cu(I) window of Cu(II)3BTC2, enabling proton-coupled, inner-sphere single-electron transfer at Cu paddlewheel nodes. Hydroquinone gives the most controlled material, [p-Ph(OH)2]-Cu3BTC2, containing 33.4% Cu(I), ship-in-a-bottle [Cu(MeCN)4]+ complexes, mesopores, and enhanced stability under humid, acidic, and basic conditions. As a heterogeneous catalyst for hydrative amide synthesis, [p-Ph(OH)2]-Cu3BTC2 affords 92% yield, negligible Cu leaching, five-cycle recyclability, and the highest turnover number among compared Cu(I) catalysts.

title: Hydroxyl‐Orchestrated Crystallization and Affinity Sites in Covalent Organic Framework Membranes for One‐Step Selective Ternary Ion Separation
abstract: ABSTRACT One‐step selective separation of multiple coexisting ions from complex aqueous media remains a formidable challenge. Here we report hydroxyl‐orchestrated covalent organic framework (COF) membranes that couple framework crystallization with hydrazone‐carbonyl pocket‐site formation, enabling ternary separation of Cs + , Sr 2+ and UO 2 2+ in a single step. Hydroxyl substitution decelerates interfacial polymerization while reinforcing intralayer hydrogen bonding to stabilize ordered frameworks, yielding high crystallinity. Concurrently, hydroxyl‐orchestrated enol‐imine to keto‐enamine tautomerization promotes the formation of hydrazone‐carbonyl pocket sites for selective UO 2 2+ chelation. The optimized membrane achieves a UO2 2+ uptake of 336 mg g −1 and a Cs + permeation flux of 0.26 mol m −2 h −1 , while exhibiting suppressed Sr 2+ permeation. Under ternary conditions, Cs + /Sr 2+ and Cs + /UO 2 2+ separation factors reach 81.5 and 326.9, with stable performance over repeated cycles. These findings establish hydroxyl‐orchestrated crystallization and pocket‐site engineering as a powerful approach for multi‐component ion separations.

title: Bioinspired Ångström-Scale Coupling of Reductive Centers in Covalent Organic Frameworks Drives Efficient Photocatalytic Oxygen Reduction
abstract: Abstract The photocatalytic oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is crucial for solar-to-chemical energy conversion but faces challenges from weak oxygen adsorption and slow kinetics. Inspired by the spatially cooperative multimetal centers in natural enzymes, we develop a strategy of Å-scale spatial coupling of reductive centers in covalent organic frameworks (COFs). Ortho-amino-functionalized COFs were constructed with catalytic pockets that position multiple acceptors within subnanometer proximity, creating coupled reductive centers for cooperative O2 adsorption and multielectron relay. The optimal framework, with a model-derived separation of approximately 3.3 Å between reductive centers, achieves a hydrogen peroxide production rate of 4.10 mmol g–1 h–1 in pure water under visible light without sacrificial agents, along with a high apparent quantum yield of 19.2% at 450 nm. Practical viability is confirmed through operation in diverse water sources and continuous-flow systems. Moreover, the enhanced ORR activity accelerates oxidative coupling of benzylamine derivatives, showing over 80% conversion for 12 analogues. Experimental and theoretical analyses indicate that the confined neighboring sites enhance O2 adsorption and activation, stabilize •OOH intermediates, and promote the two-electron reduction pathway. This work establishes convergent multicenter coupling as a foundational design principle, unlocking new avenues for the rational creation of high-performance photocatalysts in sustainable chemistry.

title: Programmable Multiplexed DNA Self‐Assembly Enables Combinatorial Gene Regulation
abstract: ABSTRACT DNA self‐assembly has emerged as a powerful tool for biosensing, nanomachinery, and gene regulation. Nevertheless, conventional hybridization chain reaction (HCR) systems predominantly adopt a single‐input‐single‐output design, which severely restricts their capacity to generate multiple intracellular regulatory outputs. Herein, we report the development of a programmable multiplexed hybridization chain reaction (mHCR) system that converts a single microRNA (miRNA) input into multiple DNA assembly pathways. Using the breast cancer‐associated miRNA‐1246 as the endogenous trigger, the mHCR system activates multiple orthogonal HCR modules through rational hairpin design, enabling efficient 1‐to‐n signal amplification. The probes were delivered by polydopamine‐modified zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO@PDA), which facilitate probe loading, cellular uptake, and intracellular release. By further incorporating DNAzyme modules, we constructed a miRNA‐responsive mHCR‐DNAzyme platform for combinatorial regulation of three cancer‐related genes (EGR1, VEGFA, and Survivin) in MCF‐7 cells. Upon intracellular miRNA‐1246 activation, the platform restored DNAzyme activity and enabled coordinated mRNA cleavage, leading to simultaneous downregulation of the three target genes. This multiplexed strategy induced 62.94% apoptosis, significantly outperforming single‐gene targeting. These results establish a programmable DNA self‐assembly platform for miRNA‐triggered combinatorial gene regulation and provide a versatile approach for engineering multifunctional nucleic acid networks in living cells.

title: Antibody-Guided Photocatalytic Cross-Linking Enables Targeted Protein Structure Elucidation
abstract: Abstract The structure and dynamics of proteins underlie virtually all biological processes, and there is a growing need for methods that can interrogate protein conformations in complex mixtures. Chemical cross-linking mass spectrometry (XL-MS) addresses this need. Still, it relies on untargeted, diffusible cross-linkers that react with any accessible residue, limiting both selectivity and effective use of cross-linking capacity. Here, we report an antibody-guided, photocatalytic cross-linking platform that enables targeted structural elucidation of proteins of interest within complex samples. We developed HyProX, a trifunctional histidine-specific cross-linker that combines two hydrazide groups to trap light-induced histidine intermediates and a phosphonic acid handle for enrichment. Building on LUX-MS photocatalytic proximity labeling, singlet oxygen generators (SOGs) conjugated to antibodies locally convert histidines on the target protein into short-lived endoperoxide intermediates, which HyProX selectively captures to form His–His cross-links in a strictly light-dependent manner. Using model peptides, we demonstrate efficient formation of cross-linked products and show that HyProX forms a C–N bond that undergoes preferential collision-induced dissociation (CID), releasing signature fragment pairs that MS3 can directly sequence. Applying antibody-guided HyProX cross-linking to human transferrin in a multiprotein mixture and human serum yields an increase in cross-linked spectral matches and higher unique cross-link coverage for the target protein compared to untargeted conditions, with all observed cross-links mapping on the known crystal structure. Together, these results establish antibody-guided, photocatalytic His–His cross-linking with HyProX as a conceptually new XL-MS platform that provides spatiotemporal control, residue selectivity, and an intrinsic MS-based decross-linking readout for targeted protein structure analysis in complex biological mixtures.

title: Tackling Lithium Transport Barriers for High‐Performance All‐Solid‐State Li 2 S Batteries With a Dual‐Functional Cathode Additive
abstract: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state Li 2 S batteries (ASSLSBs) have garnered significant attention due to their high theoretical energy density and ability to mitigate issues such as the polysulfide shuttle effect and volume expansion of sulfur cathodes. However, Li 2 S cathodes still encounter several challenges, including sluggish reaction kinetics and poor ion transport. To address these challenges, a vanadium nitride and nitrogen‐doped carbon (VN‐NC) dual‐functional additive was developed for the Li 2 S cathode in all‐solid‐state Li‐S batteries. VN‐NC exhibited a reduced energy barrier for Li 2 S conversion and promoted the in situ formation of a highly conductive LiN x O y phase, enhancing both reaction kinetics and Li + transport. As a result, the VN‐NC/Li 2 S composite achieved a peak capacity of 2.1 mAh cm − 2 with stable operation for almost 2000 cycles. More importantly, a high‐loading cathode (10 mg cm − 2 ) achieved a high areal capacity of 11.6 mAh cm − 2 while maintaining good performance for 100 cycles. This high‐performance cathode design presents a promising strategy for advancing the development of ASSLSBs.

title: Synergistic Water‐Deficient Inner Helmholtz Plane and Asymmetric Dual‐Site Nonmetal Catalysts Enable Stable Ah‐Level Aqueous Zn–I 2 Batteries at Elevated Temperatures
abstract: ABSTRACT At elevated temperatures, intensified water‐induced side reactions and iodine dissolution severely hinder the development of aqueous zinc–iodine batteries. Herein, a marginally hydrophilic and conductive modification layer with a hexagonal layered structure is constructed to stabilize the anode interface. This approach establishes a water‐deficient inner Helmholtz plane and reduces the fraction of weak hydrogen bonds, thereby suppressing spontaneous Zn dissolution and water decomposition. Concurrently, interfacial electronic structure regulation increases the energy barrier for the hydrogen evolution reaction and promotes uniform Zn deposition along the Zn‐(002) crystal plane, effectively inhibiting dendrite growth. These effects are corroborated by theoretical calculations and in situ characterizations. Furthermore, asymmetric dual‐site nonmetal single‐atom–cluster structures are introduced into the cathode host to enhance iodine adsorption and accelerate conversion kinetics, thereby mitigating iodine dissolution. Benefiting from this synergistic design, the assembled coin‐type battery delivers a discharge capacity of 95 mAh g −1 after 60 000 cycles at 8 A g −1 . A sub‐ampere‐hour‐level plastic‐cased battery employing a high‐loading cathode with a theoretical areal‐capacity of 5.6 mAh cm −2 further demonstrates strong practical potential by maintaining excellent cycling stability at 3 C and at 50°C. An Ah‐level pouch battery also exhibits stable operation at 50°C.

title: Dual Charge Extraction Pathways at Perovskite/Organic Hetero‐Contacts for Optoelectronics
abstract: ABSTRACT Charge extraction at the hetero‑contact between perovskites and organic charge‑transport layers (OCTLs) is central to the performance of perovskite optoelectronic devices, yet the microscopic mechanisms governing this process remain insufficiently resolved. Here we indicate a hybrid interfacial state that emerges broadly at perovskite/OCTL hetero‐contacts containing heteroatoms capable of coordinating to surface Pb 2+ sites. Using ultrafast spectroscopy supported by electronic‑structure calculations, we determine the energetic position and temporal evolution of this state and show that it mediates an additional, fast charge‑extraction pathway alongside the conventional valence‑band route. This dual‑pathway mechanism helps overcome interfacial energy barriers and large valence band maximum‐highest occupied molecular orbital (VBM‐HOMO) offsets that typically limit extraction efficiency. Our findings establish a general coordination‑driven origin for hybrid interfacial states and provide design principles for engineering charge‑selective contacts in next‑generation perovskite optoelectronic devices.

title: Halide‐Based Mixed Ionic‐Electronic Conductors Deliver High‐Rate and Long‐Life All‐Solid‐State Lithium Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial side reactions and degradation of solid–solid contact limit the rate capability and cycling stability of composite cathodes in all‐solid‐state lithium batteries. Here, we introduce C5.5Mo (LiMo 2 O 2.75 Cl 5.5 ), a functional halide oxide additive designed to maintain solid–solid contact, improve charge transport, and regulate the composite‐cathode interface. Its mixed ionic‐electronic conductivity and low Young's modulus promote a dense cathode microstructure and stable interparticle contact during cycling. Bias‐dependent electrochemical impedance spectroscopy of composite‐cathode symmetric cells reveals lower interfacial resistance and reduced bias sensitivity, suggesting partial alleviation of space‐charge‐layer‐related transport limitations. The full‐cell system still provides a specific capacity of approximately 100 mAh g −1 at 6 C and maintains stable cycling for 20 000 cycles (capacity retention of 85.84%). This work establishes a practical additive strategy for constructing high‐rate and long‐life composite cathodes.

title: Programming PEDOT:PSS Architecture and Gelation via Binary Eutectic Liquid–Driven Interfacial Assembly
abstract: ABSTRACT Water‐soluble electrolytes, including ionic liquids, promote PEDOT:PSS gelation by screening interparticle electrostatic repulsions, necessitating precise tuning of ionic strength in homogeneous aqueous systems. Timed electrolyte release in aqueous systems is therefore essential for directing gel formation into designed architecture and enhancing its electrical properties, yet effective strategies remain limited. This work introduces a previously unreported liquid–liquid interfacial assembly platform based on binary hydrophobic eutectic liquids (HEL), in which interfacial PEDOT:PSS–HEL complexation directs aqueous‐phase morphology and triggers subsequent gelation of PEDOT:PSS. By varying the hydrogen‐bond acceptor while maintaining a constant hydrogen‐bond donor, the ionic character of the HEL is tuned to regulate interfacial assembly. Simultaneously, hydrogen‐bonding interactions within the HEL limit electrolyte migration into the aqueous phase, thereby triggering PEDOT:PSS gelation while suppressing phase separation associated with rapid electrolyte release. This controlled interfacial process suppresses Rayleigh–Plateau instabilities and enables depth‐propagating gelation throughout the aqueous bulk, providing a versatile route to architected, high‐performance PEDOT:PSS gels, including chemically programmed liquid‐to‐gel temporal devices.

title: Corona-Length Dependence of Equilibrium Fusion and Fragmentation Energy Barriers in Block Copolymer Micelles
abstract: Abstract Fusion and fragmentation are intrinsic dynamic pathways in block copolymer micelles, governing both structural transformations and the transport of solubilized molecules. Yet, how the macromolecular architecture controls their energetic barriers remains poorly understood. In particular, while the influence of the core-forming block has been investigated, the contribution of the corona remains less explored, especially for fusion under equilibrium conditions. Here, this contribution is examined by quantifying equilibrium fusion and fragmentation kinetics in aqueous Pluronic PEO–PPO–PEO micelles from the time-resolved intermicellar exchange of an extremely hydrophobic fluorescent probe. A systematic series of copolymers with comparable PPO block lengths and PEO blocks spanning approximately 17–140 EO units was examined in the spherical-micelle regime and combined with previously reported data for copolymers spanning a broader range of PPO block lengths. Increasing the corona length produces only weak changes in both fusion and fragmentation rates, in marked contrast to the much stronger dependence on core length. The apparent activation energies for fusion and fragmentation are remarkably similar in magnitude and exhibit closely related dependences on block architecture. For both processes, this dependence is described by a common scaling form, ΔEapp ∝ NcoreaNcoronab, with a ≈ 1.3–2 and b close to zero. These results demonstrate that the energetic cost of equilibrium fusion and fragmentation is governed predominantly by the micellar core.

title: Stress-Redistributing Elastomer-Infiltrated Porous OMIEC Networks for Mechanically Robust Organic Electrochemical Transistors
abstract: Abstract Stretchable organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) require mechanically robust organic mixed ionicelectronic conductors (OMIECs) that can maintain stable ion-electron coupling under large mechanical deformation. However, although porous OMIEC architectures are advantageous for enhancing ion transport and deformability, they remain mechanically vulnerable because deformation-induced stress concentrates at pore-interconnecting regions, triggering crack initiation and propagation. Here, we develop an elastomer-infiltrated porous semiconductor (EIPS) strategy to reinforce mechanically fragile OMIEC films through the formation of an interpenetrating semiconductor-elastomer network. Ordered porous OMIEC films are constructed via a hydrophobic-additive-assisted breath-figure assembly, followed by elastomer infiltration to enable efficient mechanical load transfer and stress redistribution throughout the porous framework. Finite-element analysis reveals that elastomer infiltration homogenizes tensile stress distribution, reduces stress concentration at pore walls, and delays crack evolution during deformation. Consequently, the crack-onset strain increases substantially from 14.0 ± 4.2% for bare porous OMIEC films to 44.0 ± 4.2% for EIPS films, enabling EIPS OECTs to remain operational at a maximum tested tensile strain of 80%. Furthermore, the EIPS-based OECT platform demonstrates reliable bioelectronic functionalities, including non-invasive glucose sensing and electrophysiological signal monitoring, under mechanically deformed conditions. These results establish elastomer infiltration as an effective interface-engineering strategy for constructing mechanically resilient OMIEC architectures and advancing robust stretchable organic bioelectronics.

title: Sliding vs. Displacement Ferroelectrics: Insights From Multimodal Scanning Probe Microscopy
abstract: ABSTRACT Sliding ferroelectricity provides a route for polarization control in two‐dimensional systems that fundamentally differs from conventional displacement‐type mechanisms. However, a direct comparative study of these two distinct ferroelectric mechanisms within the same experimental framework, particularly regarding their local switching kinetics and surface screening behavior, has remained elusive. Here, prototypical sliding ferroelectric twisted hexagonal boron nitride (t‐hBN) is contrasted with conventional ferroelectric (BiFeO 3 /BFO, CuInP 2 S 6 /CIPS). Both of Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy (KPFM) and Piezoresponse Force Microscopy (PFM) were employed to compare these three systems in terms of local polarization response, surface electrostatic behavior and electric‐field‐controlled dynamics. In BFO and CIPS displacement‐type, KPFM reveals an indistinctive surface potential contrast between opposite domains, indicating dominate effect of injected and screened charges rather than intrinsic polarization charge. Their polarization reversal is characterized by PFM, which proceeds through a conventional nucleation‐and‐growth process. In contrast, KPFM resolves a pronounced surface potential difference between adjacent domains, suggesting dominate contribution of interlayer charge redistribution. Moreover, electric‐field‐driven polarization rearrangement in t‐hBN occurs predominantly through the migration of pre‐existing domain walls. These findings establish weak sensitivity to surface screening and domain‐wall‐mediated switching as characteristic features of sliding ferroelectricity, and provide fundamental insight into a mechanism distinct from conventional displacement‐type ferroelectrics.

title: Designing Vapor Highways in Porous Membranes for Scalable and Efficient Atmospheric Water Harvesting
abstract: ABSTRACT The atmosphere is a vast reservoir of freshwater. However, efficient atmospheric water harvesting (AWH) under arid conditions remains unrealized at scale due to the lack of sorbents that simultaneously deliver high capacity, rapid kinetics, and low‐cost manufacturability. Here, we present a continuous roll‐to‐roll manufacturing strategy for high‐performance AWH membranes, integrating molecular design, directional transport architecture, and industrial processability into a single scalable platform. Using a polysulfone‐ block ‐polyethylene glycol (PSF‐ b ‐PEG) block copolymer, instantaneous phase separation produces flat‐sheet membranes with vertically aligned hollow microchannels that act as vapor highways for accelerated diffusion. A brief exposure to LiCl solution triggers selective swelling of the PSF matrix, sealing surface pores while confining LiCl within the channels and effectively suppressing leakage. The resulting membranes achieve high water uptake (1.30‐4.57 g g −1 across 30–90% RH), fast sorption kinetics, and >99% capacity retention over 220 h of cycling, outperforming most reported sorbents made by batch processes. Critically, the process operates at >700 m 2 day −1 with a production cost below $14 m −2 . Outdoor tests further demonstrate reliable water harvesting performance under natural sunlight and ambient conditions. This work presents a continuous and scalable manufacturing strategy compatible with industrial production, offering an affordable, solar‐driven pathway to decentralized freshwater production.

title: A Three-Dimensional Bimetallic Triazolate Metal–Organic Framework as a Conductive Electrode for High-Performance Solid-State Supercapacitors
abstract: Abstract Herein, we report the rational design of a three-dimensional ultramicroporous bimetallic triazolate framework, FeCo-(triz)2, constructed by integrating redox-active Fe and Co centers within a robust triazolate network. The synergistic electronic interaction between the Fe and Co nodes increases the density of accessible redox-active sites while facilitating rapid electron transport and enhanced charge-transfer kinetics. Simultaneously, the strong coordination between the triazolate ligands and bimetallic nodes imparts exceptional structural and chemical stability under electrochemical operating conditions. The interconnected ultramicroporous architecture, combined with multiple accessible Fe/Co oxidation states and intrinsic electrical conductivity, promotes efficient electrolyte infiltration and accelerated ion diffusion throughout the framework. As a result, the FeCo-(triz)2 electrode delivers a high specific capacitance of 926 F g–1 at a current density of 1 A g–1 and retains 57% of its capacitance with a Coulombic efficiency of 99% at 5 A g–1 after 3000 galvanostatic charge–discharge cycles. Furthermore, an all-solid-state asymmetric supercapacitor assembled using conducting additive-free FeCo-(triz)2 as the cathode exhibits a specific capacitance of 60 F g–1 at 1 A g–1, with an energy density of 8.6 Wh kg–1 at a power density of 7731 W kg–1, outperforming many previously reported MOF- and carbon-based electrodes. The device also demonstrates remarkable long-term durability, retaining 87.5% of its initial capacitance with a Coulombic efficiency of 98.33% after 10,000 charge–discharge cycles at 5 A g–1. These findings establish the bimetallic triazolate strategy as an effective approach for overcoming the intrinsic limitations of MOF electrodes and highlight FeCo-(triz)2 as a robust and efficient electrode material for next-generation solid-state energy-storage devices.

title: Deterministic Porous Dielectrics Through Microfluidic Building‐Block Assembly for Enhanced Pressure Transduction
abstract: ABSTRACT Porous dielectrics offer an effective route to enhance electromechanical transduction in flexible capacitive sensors, yet their architectures are typically governed by stochastic pore‐forming processes, limiting control over structural and dielectric responses. Here, we develop a microfluidic building‐block assembly strategy for constructing deterministic MWCNT/MXene@PDMS porous dielectrics. Monodisperse composite microspheres are generated through microfluidic confinement and assembled into interconnected three‐dimensional networks, enabling systematic regulation of microsphere dimensions and porosity. Under compression, structural deformation is coupled with enhanced interfacial polarization and dynamic microcapacitive interactions between MWCNT/MXene nanofillers, collectively amplifying the pressure‐dependent dielectric response. The resulting sensor achieves a sensitivity of 0.1889 kPa −1 at 0–5 kPa, a detection limit of 3 Pa, and a working range up to 365 kPa, together with stable cyclic performance. Its reproducible electromechanical response further enables human‐motion and plantar‐pressure monitoring, machine‐learning‐assisted pressure‐pattern recognition, and Morse‐code‐based nonverbal communication. This work establishes microfluidic building‐block assembly as a route from stochastic pore formation to deterministic porous dielectrics, linking mesoscale structural control with dielectric modulation and functional pressure transduction.

title: Carbon-neutral algal bloom management via algal organic matter repurposing
abstract: Abstract Algal organic matter (AOM) has been considered a typical pollutant in algal bloom waters, conventionally managed through flocculation-flotation processes with high carbon footprints. This study presents a paradigm shift by redefining AOM as a functional crosslinker and developing an AOM-induced self-driven flotation (A-SDF) strategy. The approach utilizes active groups in AOM (-COOH/-OH) coordinated with trace amounts of metal coagulants to construct multilevel gel flocs with Al 2 O 3 /FeO(OH) crystalline phases. Remarkably, these flocs not only capture algal cells but also activate dissolved oxygen (DO), inducing DO enrichment-interfacial gas nucleation behavior (DOE-IGNB) and leading to microbubbles (MBs) formation at the floc interface under mild turbulence. The process achieved efficient removal of algal cells (82–95%), turbidity (86–95%), and AOM (45–79%) within 2 min without external aeration. Compared with existing technologies, the carbon footprint, treatment time, and economic cost were reduced by 66.08–96.90%, 71.67–96.00%, and 50.55–97.67%, respectively, while residual metal concentrations remained well below drinking water standards. Density functional theory calculations confirmed strong DO adsorption by tetrahedral AlO 4 /FeO 4 lattices as the molecular mechanism driving DOE-IGNB. By repurposing AOM as a resource and activating endogenous DO, this work provides a universal carbon-neutral pathway for sustainable algal bloom management worldwide.

title: Biomineralized Yeast‐DNAzyme System Enables Macrophage Immune Remodeling and Tumor Metabolic Modulation for Lung Tumor Therapy
abstract: ABSTRACT The therapeutic efficacy against lung malignancies is severely constrained by dense physiological delivery barriers and a multifaceted immunosuppressive microenvironment. Herein, we report an inhalation‐based, biomineralized yeast‐DNAzyme (MYD) platform designed for site‐specific, multi‐pathway immunotherapy. By harnessing the innate intracellular biomineralization of yeast, we successfully encapsulated magnesium ions (Mg 2+ ) as catalytic cofactors and subsequently covalently anchored miR‐21‐responsive DNAzymes to the yeast cell wall. Upon nebulized administration, this engineered yeast platform exhibits superior pulmonary enrichment and efficient targeting of tumor‐associated macrophages (TAMs), mediated by the yeast's inherent pathogen‐associated molecular patterns (PAMPs). Intracellularly, miR‐21 overexpression triggers the unlocking of Locked‐DNAzyme (LDz), and release of Mg 2+ cofactors, orchestrating a precise gene‐silencing cascade that degrades arginase‐1 ( Arg1) mRNA to drive M2‐to‐M1 macrophage repolarization. Simultaneously, the metabolically active yeast contributes to marked local glucose content depletion (by approximately 94.6%) within the tumor microenvironment, thereby inducing metabolic stress in tumor cells. This integrated strategy, combining biomimetic assembly with immune‐metabolic reprogramming, achieved significant inhibition of tumor growth in an experimental lung metastasis model, providing a potent paradigm for the targeted treatment of lung tumors.

title: Spatial Steric Regulation Enables Nucleation Site Dilution in Wide‐Bandgap Perovskite for Tandem Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Wide‐bandgap (WBG) perovskite solar cells (PSCs), essential for tandem photovoltaics, suffer from voltage losses driven by non‐radiative recombination at buried interfaces. While molecular engineering improves energy alignment and carrier extraction, the role of molecular spatial configuration in heterogeneous nucleation remains unclear. To address this, we propose a nucleation‐site‐dilution strategy using a bulky multifunctional molecule, 3T2CBN, to spatially regulate nucleation at the buried interface. The abundant tert‐butyl groups of 3T2CBN generate steric hindrance that reduces the density of active nucleation centers, thereby increasing the nucleation barrier and moderating crystallization kinetics. Consequently, this spatial and chemical modulation relaxes interfacial strain and suppresses electron leakage while ensuring efficient hole extraction. As a result, the optimized 1.8 eV WBG PSC achieves an open‐circuit voltage ( V OC ) of 1.325 V and a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.69% with enhanced stability. Moreover, this strategy enables perovskite/organic tandem solar cells to reach a competitive PCE of 26.60%. This molecular spatial regulation offers a new pathway to overcoming voltage losses in high‐efficiency tandem photovoltaics.

title: Facile Ink‐Based Fabrication of Highly Oriented Crystalline Metal–Organic Framework Thin Films
abstract: ABSTRACT Various ink‐based approaches, such as precursor‐based printing and aerosol‐jet printing, have been developed for the fabrication of metal–organic framework (MOF) thin films. However, previous studies have mainly focused on film deposition and patterning, whereas the fabrication of highly oriented MOF thin films from MOF nanosheet inks remains underexplored. Here, we present an ink‐based approach for the fabrication of highly oriented crystalline MOF thin films using Cu 2 (CuTCPP) nanosheets [H 4 (H 2 TCPP) = meso ‐tetra(4‐carboxyphenyl)porphyrin]. The Cu 2 (CuTCPP) nanosheets were dispersed in a stable colloidal solution to serve as an ink suitable for solution processing and direct writing. This ink enabled the facile fabrication of highly oriented crystalline MOF thin films on various substrates and allowed simple maskless writing. Thin‐film x‐ray diffraction measurements confirmed the high crystallinity and high degree of out‐of‐plane ( c‐ axis) orientation of the obtained films. Angle‐dependent electron spin resonance measurements revealed an anisotropic spin response, demonstrating that the preferential orientation of Cu(II) porphyrin units directly translates into direction‐dependent spin properties. These results demonstrate that colloidal MOF nanosheet ink provides an effective strategy for constructing highly oriented crystalline MOF thin films, with direct writing as an additional processing capability, thereby offering potential for future MOF‐based devices and surface engineering.

title: Dopamine‐Based Covalent Organic Framework as an Electrochemical Sensor Toward Noninvasive Early Detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Infection
abstract: ABSTRACT Pseudomonas aeruginosa is associated with morbidity and mortality in patients suffering from cystic fibrosis, making its early detection and eradication essential to reduce mortality. Therefore, development of new and improved non‐invasive sensing techniques is key for the detection and treatment of such diseases. The use of breath analysis techniques, such as the exhaled breath condensate, paired with the development of electrochemical sensor with high sensibility makes them a promising candidate to diagnose respiratory diseases. Herein we report a modified covalent organic framework with a dopamine‐derivative‐based electrochemical sensor for detection of HCN, a biomarker for the presence of Pseudomonas aeruginosa in the airways of patients with cystic fibrosis. We study the interaction of the catechol derivative present in the pores of the material with the HCN via DFT calculations, understanding the sensing interaction, and we successfully apply it to the analysis of exhaled breath samples.

title: AIE‐Active MOFs With Biomimetic Single‐Atom Zn‒N Sites for Enhanced Organophosphate Hydrolysis and Self‐Reporting Pesticide Detection
abstract: ABSTRACT Organophosphate hydrolases‐like nanozymes are promising artificial alternatives to natural organophosphate hydrolases in enzyme‐driven smart response systems; however, their performance is limited by the lack of precise spatial arrangement of Lewis acid active sites. To address this, we developed a ligand‐driven spatial programming platform that enables uniform distribution of Lewis acid sites via post‐coordination metal orientation implantation strategy. Specifically, the 4,4′,4″,4‴‐(pyrazine‐2,3,5,6‐tetrayl)tetrabenzoic acid(H 4 PTTBPC) ligand was selected as the functional building block of metal–organic framework (MOFs, Zr‐PTTBPC), with its predefined pyrazine nitrogen sites serving as anchoring centers for Lewis acid Zn species. Upon Zn incorporation, these anchoring centers enable precise guidance, uniform distribution, and spatial isolation of the Zn sites. Consequently, the Zr‐PTTBPC‐Zn with ligand‐defined Zn─N site exhibits an approximately 7.6‐fold increase in Lewis acid site concentration and a 6.4‐fold enhanced organophosphate hydrolases‐like activity compared with those of the parent Zr‐PTTBPC. Moreover, the aggregation‐induced emission (AIE) property of H 4 PTTBPC endows Zr‐PTTBPC‐Zn with bright fluorescence. Owing to its superior organophosphate hydrolases‐like activity and inherent fluorescence responsiveness, Zr‐PTTBPC‐Zn achieves colorimetric and fluorescent dual‐mode sensing of organophosphorus pesticides in various application scenarios. This work provides an effective strategy for designing high‐performance nanozymes and developing enzyme‐driven smart sensing platforms.

title: Recent Advances in Mesoporous Catalysts for Polyolefin Upcycling
abstract: Abstract Polyolefins account for the largest fraction of global plastic production, yet traditional disposal methods like landfilling and incineration cause severe pollution and resource waste. Chemical upcycling offers a promising route to transform waste polyolefins into value-added products; however, the efficient conversion of bulky polymer chains remains challenging due to mass-transfer limitations and restricted control over catalytic environments. Characterized by high specific surface areas, large pore sizes, tunable pore structures, and easily functionalized surfaces, mesoporous materials offer unique opportunities for addressing these challenges. This outlook systematically reviews the recent advances in mesoporous catalysts for four prevalent polyolefin upcycling strategies: catalytic cracking/hydrocracking, hydrogenolysis, selective oxidation, and emerging tandem/coupling technologies. We specifically summarize the critical bottlenecks of each process and highlight the pivotal roles of mesoporous catalysts in overcoming these limitations. Furthermore, the structure–activity relationships of these catalysts are discussed, followed by insights into the future design of advanced mesoporous catalytic systems.

title: Catalytic performance of hierarchically porous catalysts with various distributions of micropores and mesopores during pyrolysis of oleic acid
abstract: Abstract Non-edible lipids are a significant source of renewable liquid biofuels to mitigate CO2 emissions, especially for production of sustainable aviation fuels. The pathway of catalytic pyrolysis can convert lipids to sustainable liquid biofuels under mild reaction conditions without H2 consumption. However, it is hindered by quick deactivation of catalysts due to coking and inflexible selectivity of liquid product fractions. In this study, hierarchically porous zeolites were developed via the alkaline treatment and template methods. The relationship between the composition of liquid biofuels and the distribution of micropores and mesopores in hierarchically porous catalysts was discussed emphatically. The comprehensive characterization of catalysts confirmed the hierarchically porous structure with different volume ratios of micropore and mesopore (1:0.18–1:4) and average pore size distribution (1.99–6.24 nm). Composition of liquid biofuels obtained from catalytic pyrolysis with these hierarchically porous catalysts was also analyzed. A high kerosene selectivity (more than 40% for C10–C14) was obtained for the hierarchically porous catalyst SA-ZM-0.5 with a volume ratio (1:0.39) of micropore and mesopore during catalytic pyrolysis of oleic acid. For the catalyst series with different pore size distribution, the catalyst SB-ZM-II exhibited 79.87% selectivity for C5–C9 fractions with the maximum specific surface area (724 m2∙g-1) and the maximum mesoporous volume (0.90 cm3·g-1). The catalytic pyrolysis for conversion of non-edible lipids into liquid hydrocarbons involves a series of reactions such as cracking, deoxygenation, and carbon chain modification through aromatization and isomerization, which need deep research with simulation and model compounds.

title: Functionalised biocompatible and biodegradable amphiphilic block copolymer particles produced by self-assembly and electrospraying for biomedical applications
abstract: The work presented in this thesis focuses on the preparation of biocompatible and biodegradable amphiphilic block copolymer nanostructures suitable for biomedical applications. These polymers were prepared using a combination of reversible addition fragmentation chain-transfer (RAFT) polymerisation and ring opening polymerisation (ROP). These methods were combined in a simultaneous process under bulk conditions. Functional monomers were used to incorporate various properties into polymer chains, and particles were formed using self-assembly and electrospraying techniques. Chapter 1 describes the ROP and RAFT polymerisation processes and the suitability of these polymer materials in a biomedical setting, including the delivery of cancer treatments and gene therapy. Chapter 2 covers the synthesis of a variety of amphiphilic block copolymers through the combined ROP-RAFT polymerisation process. This was achieved using a bifunctional ROP-RAFT agent containing an -OH group capable of acting as a ROP initiator. Amphiphilic block copolymers contained either poly(trimethylene carbonate) (PTMC) or poly(lactide) (PLA) as a biodegradable hydrophobic block prepared via ROP. A range of monomers were used to synthesise the hydrophilic block via RAFT polymerisation, including biocompatible oligo(ethylene glycol methyl ether methacrylate) (OEGMA) or 2-methacryloyloxyethyl phosphorylcholine (MPC), cationic 2-(dimethylamino)ethyl methacrylate (DMAEMA) for DNA complexation, and functional monomers 4-formylphenyl methacrylate (FPMA) or methacrylic acid N-hydroxysuccinimide ester (NHSMA) for conjugation of biomolecules. In Chapter 3 a set of these polymers were selected for the preparation of nanoparticles by selfassembly. Solvent switch and thin film rehydration techniques were assessed, and the resultant morphologies were found to form mainly vesicle structures. Vesicles containing DMAEMA were tested for their ability to form complexes with DNA, as well as their cytotoxicity. Polymers containing NHSMA or FPMA groups were used to attach fluorescent dyes or RGD peptide to the vesicle surface. Blends of copolymers were examined for their cytotoxicity and stability in a serum environment. Chapter 4 covers the formation of PTMC-based amphiphilic block copolymer particles by electrospraying. A range of electrospraying conditions were investigated, including polymer concentration, solvent and flow rate of PTMC-b-POEGMA block copolymers, and blends with added PTMC homopolymer. Some of these polymers also contained NHSMA or FPMA functional groups for the potential of conjugating biomolecules to the particle surface. Finally, the thesis conclusions and future work are presented in Chapter 5.

title: Modular MDO-Based Glycopolymer Assembly Assisted by Deprotection Chemistry
abstract: The integration of cyclic ketene acetal-derived polymer segments with synthetic glycopolymers provides an attractive route toward carbohydrate-functional polymeric materials with chemically distinct block architectures, yet such combinations remain comparatively underexplored. Here, we constructed three 2-methylene-1,3-dioxepane (MDO)-based glyco-block copolymers bearing mannoside, galactoside, or glucoside moieties using a common poly(MDO) macro-chain-transfer agent. Chain extension with protected glycomonomers followed by deacetylation generated amphiphilic glycopolymers, which formed spherical nanoparticles upon transfer into aqueous solution by solvent exchange. These nanoparticles were capable of loading fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC) as a model cargo while largely retaining their colloidal properties. In vitro cellular assays revealed that the FITC-loaded nanoparticles exhibited higher cell-associated fluorescence than free FITC, indicating efficient intracellular delivery. Furthermore, the three carbohydrate-bearing nanoparticles had showed favorable short-term cytocompatibility and induced concentration-dependent increases in secretion of pro-inflammatory factors interleukin-6 and tumor necrosis factor-α by macrophage. In short, this work provides a modular platform for constructing carbohydrate-based nanomaterials with potential applications in drug delivery and related biomedical applications.

title: Emerging electrochemical transformations of allenes: synthesis, functionalization, and annulation
abstract: Allenes are versatile synthetic intermediates in which orthogonal π-bonds facilitate diverse ionic, radical, and organometallic transformations. Recent advances in organic electrosynthesis have created new opportunities for both their preparation and selective functionalization under mild redox conditions. This Review evaluates electrochemical allene synthesis and conversion with particular attention to the mechanistic roles of the electrodes. Cathodic processes generate carbanions, radicals, and low-valent catalysts, whereas anodic processes enable direct substrate oxidation, mediator activation, and carbon- or heteroatom-centered radical formation. Current, potential, catalyst identity, proton source, and reactor design can thereby control regioselectivity, radical–polar crossover, CO 2 incorporation, and product topology. Cobalt-electrocatalytic annulation has emerged as a particularly well-developed area, encompassing asymmetric transformations and continuous-flow applications. Future development will benefit from broader engagement of unactivated substrates, general asymmetric allene-forming methods, reduced reliance on sacrificial cell components, and standardized reporting of electrochemical parameters.

title: Continuous Spatiotemporal Perception Through Multilayer Hierarchically Heterogeneous Interface
abstract: ABSTRACT Dynamic human‐machine interaction (HMI) spans approaching, contact, and deformation, demanding continuous perception across the entire spatiotemporal interaction process for intelligent robotic manipulation and embodied intelligence. However, existing flexible sensors, whether based on single/dual sensing modalities or mechanically stacked architectures, fail to establish a unified interfacial charge‐regulation mechanism that coordinates charge trapping, charge transport, and piezoelectric polarization, leading to discontinuous perception and intrinsic temporal blind spots across the complete HMI process. Here, we develop a multilayer hierarchically heterogeneous fibrous sensor (HMFS) by integrating MXene, BaTiO 3 (BTO) and poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) through electrospinning. Unlike conventional stacked composites, the heterogeneous fibrous architecture enables synergistic interfacial charge modulation through coupled charge trapping, charge transport and ferroelectric polarization within a unified sensing platform. Specifically, the embedded ferroelectric BTO layer functions as deep charge trapping and polarization centers to stabilize long‐range electrostatic induction and amplify piezoelectric responses, while the interconnected MXene network establishes efficient charge‐transport pathways that facilitate interfacial charge migration and alleviate charge recombination loss. This coordinated interfacial architecture enables seamless sensing from approaching to contact and subsequent deformation, integrating tele‐perception, tactile perception and pressure sensing without spatiotemporal blind spots. The resulting sensor achieves a maximum tele‐perception distance of 1.2 m, stable tactile operation over 40,000 cycles, and a pressure sensitivity of 523.6 mV kPa − 1 . Coupled with a one‐dimensional convolutional neural network, the system recognizes complete spatiotemporal interaction states with an accuracy of 92.6%. This work establishes a heterogeneous interfacial engineering strategy for continuous spatiotemporal perception, providing a unified sensing framework for next‐generation embodied intelligence, intelligent robotics and soft biomimetic HMI.

title: Enhanced Silicon Anodes via Active Interfacial Reconstruction Enabled by Additive‐Engineered Conductive Binders
abstract: ABSTRACT Silicon anodes are promising candidates for high‐energy‐density lithium‐ion batteries, but severe volume fluctuations and unstable solid electrolyte interphases (SEI) hinder their practical application. Although conductive polymer binders eliminate the need for inactive conductive additives, they usually lack sufficient interfacial adhesion and SEI‐regulating capabilities. Herein, we design an additive‐engineered conductive binder system by integrating a fluorinated additive (FS) into a PEDOT:PSS matrix, enabling an active interfacial reconstruction strategy for silicon anodes. The FS additive acts as a “molecular bridge” that anchors the binder onto the silicon surface via hydrogen bonding to reinforce interfacial adhesion, while simultaneously serving as an “electrochemical initiator” that drives the in situ evolution of a dense, LiF‐rich SEI. This dual‐functional synergy mitigates mechanical degradation and stabilizes the anode interphase. Consequently, a carbon‐free silicon anode with 90 wt.% silicon content maintains 96.6% capacity retention after 200 cycles at 400 mA g −1 and delivers 1071 mAh g −1 at a high rate of 4000 mA g −1 . Paired with an NCM811 cathode in a full cell, the system demonstrates a reversible capacity of 162 mAh g −1 with 85.4% capacity retention over 300 cycles. This work offers a practical molecular engineering pathway for developing high‐capacity, durable silicon anodes.
